title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## CT‑SGAL‑LIO: Continuous‑Time LiDAR‑Inertial Odometry Refinement

### The Breakthrough
CT‑SGAL‑LIO refines the pose output of a discrete SGal(3) LiDAR‑inertial odometry estimator by fitting a cubic spline over a recent pose window and querying it at a small lag. This causal continuous‑time interpolation yields up to 70% reduction in relative trajectory error on the GRAND‑TOUR dataset and 9.9–51.1% improvements on GEODE sequences, while cutting posterior jumps by 85.4% in a long‑duration run.

### The Caveats
The approach is only evaluated against its own unrefined discrete baseline, with no comparison to existing continuous‑time odometry methods.

## UAV‑Flow++: Language‑Guided UAV Flight Suite

### The Breakthrough
UAV‑Flow++ introduces a benchmark of over 30k real‑world and 10k simulated UAV trajectories driven by natural‑language commands, and presents FlowVLA, a policy that first imitates mixed demonstrations then refines with Tail‑Aware GRPO reinforcement. The method reaches 75.58% success on 273 simulated test episodes, rising to 93.16% after post‑training, and demonstrates feasibility on real UAVs.

### The Caveats
No comparison to prior language‑guided UAV baselines is provided, leaving the significance of the gains unclear.

## FORGE: Force‑Aware Humanoid Loco‑Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
FORGE combines a coarse‑to‑fine command hierarchy with a momentum observer corrected by a learned contact‑force model, enabling estimation of wrist‑equivalent forces from proprioception and adaptive virtual‑target loops. Experiments show stable whole‑body control and successful squat‑and‑lift tasks under varying payloads using only sparse wrist pose commands.

### The Caveats
The paper lacks baseline or ablation studies, so its advantage over existing methods is unverified.

## Grove‑G1: ROS2 Autonomy Stack for Unitree Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
The Grove‑G1 repository delivers a full ROS2 Jazzy stack that runs unchanged from simulation to the physical Unitree G1, integrating a learned 50 Hz walking policy, Nav2 navigation, MoveIt2 manipulation, and a conversational agent via BehaviorTree.CPP, enabling simultaneous walking and manipulation.

### The Caveats
Only simulation demos are shown; the stack, especially the vision‑language‑action grasping policy, has never been demonstrated on the real robot nor benchmarked against baselines.

## Cerulion: Low‑Latency ROS2 Runtime with Deterministic Replay

### The Breakthrough
Cerulion uses iceoryx2 zero‑copy shared‑memory transport to achieve a 1 MiB image round‑trip latency of 4.08 µs (p50) and 7.38 µs (p99), far faster than ROS2 Jazzy's 10.95 ms, and records execution traces in MCAP for deterministic replay that flags byte‑wise mismatches.

### The Caveats
Latency gains are reported only on a synthetic microbenchmark and have not been validated on real robot workloads or against high‑performance ROS2 middleware.

## Waymo Robotaxis: Illegal School‑Bus Passing After Fix

### The Breakthrough
Waymo issued a software update in November 2025 to modify the Waymo Driver’s behavior around stopped school buses, but NHTSA reports that most illegal‑passing incidents occurred after the update, prompting a new federal investigation.

### The Caveats
The fix was never validated with systematic real‑world testing or quantitative metrics, relying solely on incident reports and video anecdotes.

## OpenAI Robotics Team Disbanded: Shift to General Models

### The Breakthrough
OpenAI restructured its robotics effort, arguing that frontier models like GPT‑6 Astra achieved 74.8% success on a simulated manipulation benchmark, surpassing the previous 51.0% best specialized models, and will now apply these general models to embodied AI.

### The Caveats
The claim rests only on a simulated benchmark with no real‑world robot testing, latency analysis, or cloud‑dependency evaluation.

## Serve Robotics: Open Delivery‑Robot API

### The Breakthrough
Serve Robotics opened its fleet‑management, routing, and robot‑control APIs to third‑party developers, allowing external services to program tasks on its autonomous delivery robots.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no independent performance data, real‑world trials, or security analysis to substantiate reliability for developers.

## HEIR: Egocentric Intent Dataset for HRI

### The Breakthrough
HEIR supplies synchronized human speech, gaze, and egocentric video aligned with robot observations and teleoperated trajectories, enabling research on intent grounding and execution planning; experiments show performance gains when using these cues.

### The Caveats
No baseline or prior‑dataset comparisons are offered, so the reported improvements cannot be benchmarked against existing resources.

## OpenHarness: Multi‑Agent AI Coding Command Center

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness runs multiple AI coding agents side‑by‑side in tmux panes, connects machines via encrypted WebRTC with sub‑15 ms UI latency, and abstracts agents as interchangeable "harnesses" for rapid domain switching, targeting robotics developers.

### The Caveats
Its low‑latency, encrypted UI is never evaluated on real robotic hardware or compared to existing IDE or orchestration tools.

## AndroidEnv: RL Platform for Android Devices

### The Breakthrough
AndroidEnv v2 separates raw device control from RL task semantics, offering subscription‑based telemetry (screenshots, accessibility trees, sensors) and a rich action API for multi‑touch, hardware keys, text entry, and ADB commands, plus a web Playground for LLM‑driven interaction.

### The Caveats
The library lacks performance or latency benchmarks and real‑world RL experiments, leaving its practical utility unproven.

### Priority
CT‑SGAL‑LIO offers the most immediately actionable improvement for robot perception by dramatically reducing odometry error on established benchmarks.

### One action
Integrate CT‑SGAL‑LIO into your LiDAR‑inertial pipeline and evaluate its error reduction on your own datasets.
